lines.trans: Watch where you are reaching, grandson!
Grandma, quiet! Don't bother me while I look for a present!
What, did you fall in love? And who needs you like this?
What? In your day there weren't even words like that!
Nobody will like this old brooch! Not even Klavdia Viktorovna!
But Grandpa gave it to you! So there is something special about it, right?
There is nothing special about it! Grandpa worked at the factory where they made these brooches.
He took them from the factory and gave them to everyone! I never wore this brooch in my life!
Right here is where I will put it! It will be an excellent gift!
Yes, what do you want?
Arkady Borisovich, it is time for our consultation now.
Let's do it later, I'm busy! Wait in the kitchen.
Wonderful, I will wait.
Nina, hi! I stopped by to see Arkady Borisovich, but he is busy.
I brought pastries! Maybe we could have some tea in the meantime?

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence

examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: Core Russian part meaning 'even' in everyday speech.
+ dative of person + accusative of gift

examples.text: Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.

examples.text: У меня дед три года партизанил!
examples.trans: My grandfather was a partisan for three years!
My grandfather lives in the country.

examples.text: Я никого пытать не буду, ясно? У меня дед три года партизанил!
examples.trans: I'm not going to torture anyone, got it? My grandfather was a partisan for three years!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.

examples.trans: Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'life' in everyday Russian.
takes preposition на: работать на заводе

examples.text: Я всю жизнь работала на заводе.
examples.trans: I worked my whole life at the factory.

examples.text: Этот завод построили много лет назад.
examples.trans: This factory was built many years ago.

examples.text: Я всю жизнь работала на заводе. Всю жизнь!
examples.trans: I worked my whole life at the factory. My whole life!

зайти.gloss: to come in, to drop in

meanings.en: to come in, to step in

examples.trans: I'll drop by in the evening.

examples.text: Ну, как хочешь. Лидия Алексеевна, зайдите, пожалуйста!
examples.trans: Well, as you like. Lidia Alekseyevna, come in, please!

meanings.note: of a person: я занят = I'm busy
of a place: здесь занято = it's occupied
что это значит? = what does this mean?
the form значит is used as a linking word

examples.trans: Pasha, what does all this mean?

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'кать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to look for'.

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.
It is time for our consultation now.
I need a consultation with a lawyer.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, сейчас время нашей консультации.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, it is time for our consultation now.
Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: for movement; где is for location

examples.trans: Wait, where are you two going?

мешать.gloss: to be in the way, to disturb

meanings.en: to be in the way, to hinder

examples.trans: The radiators are in the way.

examples.text: Филиппыч, миксер проехать не может. Радиаторы мешают.
examples.trans: Filippych, the mixer truck can't get through. The radiators are in the way.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Core Russian pron meaning 'they' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'личный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('excellent').

examples.text: Квартира будет отличная. На Симашко есть новый дом.
examples.trans: It'll be an excellent flat. There's a new building on Simashko Street.

meanings.note: substantivized neuter adjective, declines like an adjective

examples.trans: I brought pastries! Maybe we could have some tea in the meantime?

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'арить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to give (as a present)', paired with 'дарить'.

examples.text: А вы мне тоже айфон подарите?
examples.trans: Will you give me an iPhone too?

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'арок'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'present, gift' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is a present for you.

examples.text: Это семейный праздник. Как в детстве, с подарками!
examples.trans: It's a family holiday. Like when we were kids, with presents!

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'later' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Go on, come by later! Later!

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to bring (carrying)', paired with 'приносить'.

examples.text: А я вот вам чаю с сушками принёс.
examples.trans: I've brought you some tea and bread rings.

meanings.note: работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: 'дать слово' = to give one's word, 'держать слово' = to keep one's word
'дать слово' = to give one's word, 'держать слово' = to keep one's word

examples.trans: Slavik, look here. I'll swap my new iPhone for your old phone.

meanings.note: at the start of a question

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: я что-то вижу = I see something
colloquial, used as an adverb: что-то я не вижу = somehow I don't see it
